note.p: Ed Pope notes: Entries after 1820 refer to Henry Robinson Palmer DNB 1795-1844, who worked as an assistant to Thomas Telford DNB 1757-1834, and went on to found the Institution of Ciovil Engineers. Sir H Parnel who called at Palmer's while Godwin was there in 1820 was very likely Henry Brooke Parnell DNB1776-1820 who succeeded to a baronetcy in 1816. Only the 1825 entry which had no initial H could easily have been someone else, as Palmer was a common name. It is something of a stretch to identify entries for H P with Palmer, However, there are inconsistencies in associating the entries with H Pilcher.: viz: Godwin's general practice with relatives is to refer to H and E Prentice, rather than 'HP and Prentice'. See also 19 May 1824, 'E and S Prentice and P and HP.' and 9 February 1825 'H and S Prentice and HP'. In each case this suhhests that HP is being disctinguished from Prentice. But that leaves open whether they are references ro H Pilcher or H Palmer. We have not currently coded them to H Palmer.
